solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grumbler — mean or crazy?

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters of mean or are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a habitual complainer is merely nasty or actually mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' looks like one choice in the question, but it is the signal that rearranges the letters of 'mean or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A moaner is someone who complains constantly, a grumbler by another name.

clue.text: Fashionable instant meal

parts.note: a mo is a moment
a dish is a meal or course

explanation.surface: A trendy ready meal, the kind you microwave in a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant meal' reads as one thing, but 'instant' is a noun here: a mo, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means in the current fashion.

clue.text: Paying heed at tense conclusion

parts.note: taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone listening closely as a nail-biting story reaches its climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the conclusion; it is the grammatical tense, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to attend is to listen or give heed, as in 'attend to what I say'.

clue.text: English literature, fifth of subjects chosen

definitions.note: ELITE is a noun and 'chosen' an adjective, but 'the chosen' and 'the elite' swap freely.

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
lit is short for literature

indicators.note: Fifth of a word is its fifth letter.

parts.note: the fifth letter of S-U-B-J-E-C-T-S

explanation.surface: A school timetable listing English literature as one of the subjects a pupil has chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a list of exam options; only the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the chosen few, the select best of a group.

clue.text: Improvement in Hampshire for many

indicators.note: The answer sits in the letters of the words that follow.

parts.note: hampshiRE FOR Many

explanation.surface: A local change in Hampshire that benefits many residents.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is an English county, which makes it sound like a real place is under discussion; it just houses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a reform is a change made to put something right.

clue.text: Guards heading off for gates?

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, comes off the word

parts.note: sentries are guards on watch

explanation.surface: Guards set off to take up their posts at the gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' sounds like the guards leaving, but it removes the first letter of SENTRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Entries are ways in, doors or entrances, so gates are examples of them.

clue.text: Member of Parliament depressed, first to last

definitions.note: a parliament is the collective noun for a group of these birds, so one of them is a member

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the last position

parts.note: low means depressed, down in spirits

explanation.surface: A dejected MP is shuffled from the front bench to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of Parliament' suggests a politician, but a parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls; 'first to last' moves the opening letter of LOW to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of owls is called a parliament, so each bird in it is a member of a parliament.

clue.text: Month on edge — an unsettling experience

indicators.note: In a down clue, 'on' places the first piece on top of the next.

parts.note: May is a month
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A month spent on edge, full of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as a single phrase meaning nervous; split it, and 'on' only says the month comes first in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or chaos, which leaves everyone involved shaken.

clue.text: Terribly tired in the mind, to ill effect

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly messed up, so the letters of tired are rearranged

parts.note: mentally means in the mind

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly exhausted mentally, and it is doing them harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly tired' reads as one phrase, but 'Terribly' is the anagram signal working on 'tired' alone, giving DETRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Detrimentally means in a harmful or damaging way, so with bad consequences.

clue.text: Excluding physical exercise, surprisingly I tend to be fit

parts.note: ex means without or excluding, as in ex dividend
PE is the abbreviation for physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters of I tend are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone who skips gym class claims they still manage to be fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excluding physical exercise' reads as skipping the gym, but it is two pieces: EX (without) and PE; 'surprisingly' then turns 'I tend' into DIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means suitable or convenient for the purpose, which is a sense of fit, as in fit for purpose.

clue.text: One getting left out to suffer superficial damage?

indicators.note: with out, getting left out means the left letter is removed
the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A single person left out of things suffers some minor hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One getting left out' sounds like social exclusion, but it tells you to take L out of SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn lightly on the surface, scorching without destroying, so damage that is only skin deep.

clue.text: Run into difficulty and feel a stinging sensation

indicators.note: The first piece goes into the second.

parts.note: in a pickle means in difficulty
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone who hits trouble and feels the sting of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run into difficulty' reads as one phrase; split it, R goes inside PICKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prickle is the tingling feeling of skin touched by nettles or pins.

clue.text: Depression in front of a computer screen?

definitions.meaning: the surface pushes low mood; the setter means a pressing down, as of a key

definitions.text: in front of a computer screen?
definitions.meaning: where the keyboard sits, so the thing pressed is a key

explanation.surface: A person sitting glumly at their computer, feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' is the physical pressing down of a key, not low mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystroke is a key pressed down on the keyboard in front of the screen.

clue.text: Shamelessness of my demo: it's out of order

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone admits their protest or presentation was shameless and inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as a judgement on the demo, but it signals an anagram of 'my demo it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodesty is a lack of modesty or decency, which is boldness without shame.

clue.text: Gas satisfied hotel — a new source of energy

parts.note: a need met is a need satisfied
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
E is the physics symbol for energy; 'source of' is surface padding

explanation.surface: A hotel pleased with its new gas supply as an energy source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of energy' looks like a gloss on the gas, but it just supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: methane is one gas among many, the main part of natural gas.

clue.text: A Liberal was deceitful in league with others

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
lied means was deceitful

explanation.surface: A politician caught lying while in a coalition with other parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a political scandal; the definition is only the last four words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: nations allied by treaty are in league with each other.

clue.text: Group of workers sealing terms ultimately for agreement

indicators.note: the union seals in, encloses, the following letter

parts.note: a trade union is an organised group of workers

indicators.note: only the last letter of terms is used

parts.note: last letter of terms

explanation.surface: A trade union seals the terms of a deal at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealing' has the union wrap round S, which 'ultimately' takes from the end of 'terms'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together in harmony, in full accord.

clue.text: Messenger last to see person receiving gift

parts.note: a legate is an envoy, often papal

indicators.note: Last to a word is its final letter.

parts.note: the final letter of see

explanation.surface: A courier who is the last to see the recipient of a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last to see' reads as a messenger arriving late; it is the final letter of 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee receives a legacy, a gift left in a will.

clue.text: Hit it off and made progress

definitions.meaning: to hit it off is to become friendly at once
to get on is to advance

explanation.surface: Two people who got along and moved forward together.
explanation.walkthrough: Got on means both got along with someone and advanced.
explanation.definitionFit: People who hit it off got on well; someone who made progress got on.

clue.text: Spirits dope one repeatedly

indicators.note: Repeatedly means the piece is used twice.

parts.note: gen and dope are both slang for information
I is the Roman numeral for one
the I again

explanation.surface: Someone spiking a drink with spirits again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' here is information, not drugs; gen is British slang for the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie, spirits of Arabian legend.

clue.text: Immediate sensation aunt produced somehow

indicators.note: produced by some unstated means, so the letters of sensation aunt are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt somehow causes an immediate stir.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase after 'aunt' reads as the aunt causing a stir, but it is the anagram signal: all thirteen letters of 'sensation aunt' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Instantaneous means happening in an instant, with no delay at all.

clue.text: The total amount? Just a bit of it, by the sound of it

indicators.note: What is said, not what is written.

parts.note: some means a bit of it

explanation.surface: Someone asking for the whole amount and getting only a portion.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the whole and a part are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the figure reached when everything is added up.

clue.text: Young woman belonging to Amsterdam's elite

indicators.note: The answer belongs to, sits within, the words that follow.

parts.note: amsterDAM'S ELite

explanation.surface: A young woman from Amsterdam high society.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored when reading the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old, storybook word for a young unmarried woman, as in 'damsel in distress'.

clue.text: Bird, one flying by animal on farm

indicators.note: by means next to, so the flying letters sit beside the animal, after it

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal

indicators.note: flying means scattered through the air, so the letters of one are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird flies past an animal in a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' fits a bird, but here it rearranges 'one' into EON, which 'by' sets beside PIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common plump grey bird, familiar in towns and lofts.
